abstract: People increasingly use social media to report emergencies, seek help or share information during disasters, which makes social networks an important tool for disaster management. To meet these time-critical needs, we present a weakly supervised approach for rapidly building high-quality classifiers that label each individual Twitter message with fine-grained event categories. Most importantly, we propose a novel method to create high-quality labeled data in a timely manner that automatically clusters tweets containing an event keyword and asks a domain expert to disambiguate event word senses and label clusters quickly. In addition, to process extremely noisy and often rather short user-generated messages, we enrich tweet representations using preceding context tweets and reply tweets in building event recognition classifiers. The evaluation on two hurricanes, Harvey and Florence, shows that using only 1-2 person-hours of human supervision, the rapidly trained weakly supervised classifiers outperform supervised classifiers trained using more than ten thousand annotated tweets created in over 50 person-hours.

bibliographic.title: Weakly-supervised Fine-grained Event Recognition on Social Media Texts for Disaster Management

content.problem: Supervised training of fine-grained event recognizers for individual disaster tweets needs large manually labeled datasets that take days to create, which is too slow for time-critical disaster response.
content.proposed_solution: The approach clusters keyword-matched tweets so an expert can quickly confirm pertinent word senses, then trains a multi-channel BiLSTM using context and reply tweets, and improves coverage through bootstrapping.
content.algorithm_or_model: multi-channel BiLSTM classifier with clustering-assisted word sense disambiguation labeling
dataset_testbed: Hurricane Harvey Twitter dataset (about 65k unlabeled tweets and 11,782 annotated evaluation tweets collected via the GNIP API)
Hurricane Florence Twitter dataset (about 69.8k unlabeled tweets and 4,059 annotated evaluation tweets collected via the GNIP API)

content.claim: Using only 1 to 2 person-hours of labeling effort, the weakly supervised classifiers outperform supervised classifiers trained on more than ten thousand tweets that took over 50 person-hours to annotate.

evidence.problem_quote: To facilitate disaster management, especially during the time-critical disaster response phase, it is vital to build event recognizers rapidly. However, the typical supervised learning paradigm requires a carefully labeled dataset that is normally created by asking human annotators to go through a large number of data instances and label them one by one, and the data labeling procedure usually takes days at least.
evidence.proposed_solution_quote: For fast deployment, we propose a novel data labeling method and an overall weakly supervised learning approach that quickly builds reliable fine-grained event recognizers.
evidence.claim_quote: The evaluation on two hurricanes, Harvey and Florence, shows that using only 1-2 person-hours of human supervision, the rapidly trained weakly supervised classifiers outperform supervised classifiers trained using more than ten thousand annotated tweets created in over 50 person-hours.
